title: arXiv mathematics — 28 October 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv supplies no official trending chart; the ordering is an inferred notable-paper selection, not measured popularity. Attention and citation evidence is limited for papers announced only days ago.

sections.title: Nonuniqueness of Solutions to 2D Incompressible Euler Equations with Unbounded Vorticity
sections.abstract: The author constructs two distinct finite-energy solutions of planar incompressible Euler from the same compactly supported, mean-zero initial vorticity lying in every finite Lp space, using a cascade of quadrupole transitions across scales.
sections.claimed_result: The author states that two distinct global solutions share the same initial vorticity, with vorticity in every finite Lp at all times and velocity in C([0,∞);L2); their L1 difference is positive at time 1.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced 2D Euler on R2; compactly supported, mean-zero initial vorticity in the intersection of all finite Lp spaces; the stated solutions conserve each finite-p vorticity norm.
sections.unique_caveat: The author says the construction does not establish sharpness of the quantitative Yudovich uniqueness criterion; it does not concern bounded vorticity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Concrete nonuniqueness result in a central PDE problem; introduction and theorem statement checked. Placement reflects potential mathematical significance rather than measured readership.

sections.title: Local Law and Eigenvector Delocalization for Random Lifts
sections.abstract: For random N-lifts of a fixed finite graph of minimum degree at least three, the authors prove high-probability entrywise Green-function estimates down to logarithmic-over-N scales away from singular energies, and deduce complete eigenvector delocalization there.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove Green-function control at scales (log N)^C/N and an eigenvector sup-norm bound (log N)^C/sqrt(N) with high probability.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Uniformly sampled N-lifts of a fixed finite connected simple base graph with minimum degree at least three; eigenvalues must remain a fixed positive distance from singular energies of the universal-cover spectrum.
sections.unique_caveat: Singular energies are excluded; claims are for fixed base graphs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A quantitative local law and uniform eigenvector conclusion are paired in one result, cross-listed across probability, mathematical physics, combinatorics, and spectral theory.

sections.title: All Strict Calabi--Yau Threefolds of Height One Lift to Characteristic 0
sections.abstract: The author proves that every strict Calabi–Yau threefold of Artin–Mazur height one over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic has a projective lift to characteristic zero, even with crystalline torsion and arbitrary characteristic, and gives a counterexample to an unobstructedness conjecture.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves projective liftability to W(k) for strict height-one Calabi–Yau threefolds and shows that an Addington–Bragg example has W2-lifts that fail to extend to W3.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Strict Calabi–Yau threefold over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0, with Artin–Mazur height one; no torsion-freeness assumption on crystalline cohomology.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem gives existence of a lift, not unobstructedness of the whole deformation space or a canonical lift; height two and dimensions at least four remain beyond the theorem.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Inspected introduction states a general height-one lifting theorem and an explicit counterexample to a conjecture, while distinguishing liftability from unobstructedness.

sections.title: The sharp exponent for the Banach--Mazur distance to the cube
sections.abstract: The author proves a lower bound of order n^(2/3)(log(2n))^(-10) for the maximal Banach–Mazur distance from an n-dimensional real normed space to ℓ∞^n, which matches a previously known upper bound at the exponent level and yields n^(2/3+o(1)).
sections.claimed_result: The author establishes R∞(n) ≥ c n^(2/3)(log(2n))^(-10); together with the cited prior upper bound this yields R∞(n)=n^(2/3+o(1)).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Maximal Banach–Mazur distance from n-dimensional real normed spaces to ℓ∞^n; lower-bound examples are polars of symmetric Gaussian polytopes with 2n generators.
sections.unique_caveat: The matching exponent uses an earlier upper bound, and the new lower bound retains a logarithmic loss and unspecified constant.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives a matching asymptotic exponent for a central finite-dimensional normed-space problem and describes a probabilistic construction with exponentially high probability.

sections.title: Escape of mass for finite-area hyperbolic surfaces
sections.abstract: For a noncompact finite-area hyperbolic surface, the authors give a lower bound for the L2 mass of eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series on a compact part, extending a result of Soundararajan to the nonarithmetic setting.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the stated lower bound on compact-part L2 mass for eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series; the abstract does not specify its numerical form.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Noncompact hyperbolic surface of finite area; eigenfunctions and Eisenstein series restricted to a compact part.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not state the bound’s explicit constants or parameter range; proof depends on long-time Egorov estimates and other technical inputs.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The stated extension reaches nonarithmetic surfaces and spans spectral theory, PDE, and dynamics; the abstract names the mathematical ingredients.

sections.title: Sharp Stability of Brenier Potentials and its Link to Poincaré Inequalities
sections.abstract: The authors prove a functional inequality stronger than Poincaré for uniformly log-concave measures, bounding variances of differences of convex functions and yielding sharp stability of quadratic-optimal-transport Brenier potentials under target-measure changes.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the inequality and, for Gaussian measures, recover equivalence between Bures–Wasserstein distance of positive semidefinite matrices and Frobenius distance between their square roots.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Uniformly log-concave source measure and quadratic optimal transport; stability concerns varying the target measure.
sections.unique_caveat: The stated framework is uniformly log-concave and quadratic-cost; the abstract does not claim the same stability beyond those hypotheses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Connects optimal-transport stability with functional inequalities and a Gaussian-matrix consequence; four mathematical categories provide a cross-field signal.

sections.title: High-dimensional critical percolation and critical Branching random walks are intersection equivalent
sections.abstract: In dimensions d>6, under a standard comparability assumption on the two-point and Green functions, the authors show that critical percolation and critical branching random walk have comparable probabilities of hitting a distant finite set relative to its diameter.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves the two hitting probabilities are within fixed positive multiplicative constants of one another under the stated distance condition.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Critical models on Z^d with d>6; the two-point function and Green function must be of the same order, and the finite target set must be sufficiently far away compared with its diameter.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is restricted to high dimensions and the stated comparability hypothesis; it does not cover low dimensions or arbitrary critical models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a precise comparison between two foundational critical models and gives a named proof mechanism, a truncated equilibrium measure with an approximate last-passage formula.

sections.title: Nonlinear uncertainty principle
sections.abstract: The authors prove an uncertainty principle for subsets of R under weak branching assumptions, requiring a nonlinear phase condition; without that condition, arithmetic progressions provide a failure example.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish their uncertainty principle for subsets of R satisfying weak branching and a nonlinearity condition on the phase.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Subsets of the real line with weak branching; the phase must meet the paper’s nonlinear condition.
sections.unique_caveat: The nonlinear condition is essential; the authors say this is part of work in progress, released early, and overlaps arXiv:2609.30261.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states the structural hypothesis and a concrete obstruction when it is removed, and names Shmerkin’s nonlinear projection theorem as a proof ingredient.

sections.title: Sharp helical maximal estimates in all dimensions
sections.abstract: The authors prove Lp boundedness for the maximal averaging operator along any smooth nondegenerate curve in R^n when p>n, using a weighted Kakeya-type estimate.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the displayed Lp maximal-operator estimate for every p>n and every nondegenerate curve under their stated smoothness conditions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth nondegenerate curve gamma in R^n and the associated maximal averaging operator; p must be strictly greater than n.
sections.unique_caveat: The result as stated does not cover endpoint p=n; the abstract alone does not establish endpoint failure.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a theorem for all dimensions and identifies a new weighted Kakeya-type ingredient, a specific harmonic-analysis method signal.
